items.name: AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, Insurance Component
items.use: Premiums, worker shares and deductibles by state
items.limit: Survey of private-sector employers that offer coverage, with sampling error that this site tests before calling a gap real.

items.name: U.S. Census Bureau, CPS ASEC Table H-8B
items.limit: Three-year averages, so it lags. Covers all households, not only those with employer plans.

items.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U
items.limit: The 2025 average leaves out October, when no data were collected.

items.name: CMS National Health Expenditure Accounts
items.limit: National only, about all private insurance.

items.name: CMS Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating
items.use: Hospital quality in the price lookup
items.limit: One summary of many measures. Some hospitals have too few reported measures for a rating.

items.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, state household debt
items.limit: From a credit-record panel; the U.S. line on this site is a computed weighted figure, marked as such.

items.name: HCAI Office of Health Care Affordability, spending reports
items.use: Spending per member, the state target, and regional spending
items.limit: Collected from plans. The 2023 to 2024 report is labeled interim, and totals differ from the earlier baseline report.

items.name: HCAI Hospital Measurement Combined Dataset and hospital cost dataset
items.use: The hospital price lookup and OHCA's high-cost list
items.limit: Estimated from hospitals' financial reports, not claims. Some values look implausible, so this site screens by volume and labels unusual ratios.

items.name: HCAI Hospital Annual Financial Disclosure data
items.limit: Facility reports. Some large systems sweep cash to a parent, so some facility-level measures mislead.

items.name: California Department of Managed Health Care, premium rate report
California Department of Public Health, facility listing
items.use: The exact link between state hospital IDs and CMS numbers
items.limit: An administrative list: a hospital missing a CMS number shows no rating.

items.name: Covered California, Data and Research
items.use: Links to plan and enrollment documents
items.limit: Links only; this site does not reanalyze them.

items.name: SHADAC, University of Minnesota, State Health Compare
items.use: Skipped care, trouble paying bills, health costs above 10% of income
items.limit: Processes CDC, NHIS and Census surveys. Each measure has its own years and margin of error.

items.name: RAND, Hospital Price Transparency Study, Round 5.1
items.use: National and California context for hospital prices
items.limit: Employers choose to take part, no California claims database is included, and the sample is about 6% of U.S. commercial hospital spending. Funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and participating employers.

items.name: Urban Institute, Debt in America
items.use: Medical debt in collections by state and county
items.limit: Credit records miss seven states, including California, whose laws restrict reporting.

items.name: KFF, Employer Health Benefits Survey
items.limit: Employers with 10 or more workers, public and private. A sample of firms, so it will not match the federal survey exactly.

items.name: KFF and California Health Care Foundation, California Health Benefits Survey
items.limit: 464 firms, 13% response rate, so wider margins than the federal survey.

items.name: California Health Care Foundation and NORC, California Health Policy Survey
items.use: What Californians report about skipped care and medical debt
items.limit: Self-reported, and counts family members. CalMatters, one of the newsrooms on our news lists, notes that some of its coverage is supported by CHCF, so treat the two as related rather than independent.
